conventions.convention: Local finite type requires finitely many sections on one neighborhood whose germs generate every stalk throughout that neighborhood; finite generation at just the central stalk is insufficient.

Coherence means local finite type together with local finite type of the kernel of every finite-rank free module morphism into the sheaf, on every open restriction. Rank zero denotes the zero module sheaf.

The bounded-degree lemma assumes monic polynomials of positive degrees at most d whose lower coefficients vanish at the common base center. Its conclusion holds at every point of the product polydisc, with polynomial components in w−w₀ and coefficients germwise holomorphic in the base variables.
Full Axiom of Choice is an explicit ambient assumption of the Oka theorem and both examples; the local Oka proof itself uses finite selections and finite neighborhood shrinkings.

For each prescribed finite ℓ≥0, a partial finite-rank free resolution exists on a neighborhood depending on the point, sheaf and ℓ. Exactness is asserted at the module and every free term except the leftmost; no global analytic free resolution is asserted.
The bidisc relation generator is (−z₂,z₁). The point-quotient example uses pairwise generators zⱼeᵢ−zᵢeⱼ for i<j, with the empty generating family when N=1.

load_bearing.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. On a finite-dimensional complex manifold, every finite tuple of holomorphic functions has a locally finite-type relation sheaf, so the holomorphic structure sheaf is coherent. Coherent modules are closed under kernels, cokernels and finite extensions. For every coherent module, point and finite ℓ≥0, there is a chart neighborhood with a partial finite-rank free resolution exact at the module and every free term except the leftmost.
A module sheaf is coherent if it is locally of finite type and the kernel of every morphism from a finite-rank free module sheaf on every open restriction is locally of finite type.

For the stated tuple of monic Weierstrass polynomials of degrees between 1 and d on a centered product polydisc, every relation germ at every point (x′,w₀) is generated over the full holomorphic germ ring by relation germs polynomial in w−w₀ of component degrees at most d, with coefficients in the base germ ring.
Let (X,A) be a ringed space whose structure sheaf is coherent. For all finite integers p,q≥0 and every A-module morphism A^p→A^q, the kernel sheaf is locally of finite type.

The kernel and cokernel of any morphism between coherent module sheaves on a ringed space are coherent. In every short exact sequence of module sheaves, if any two terms are coherent, then the third is coherent.

published_dependencies.used_for: The underlying space and sheaf of commutative rings in the coherence definition.
Module sheaves and their module-linear morphisms.
Objectwise kernels and sheafified images and cokernels throughout the module calculus and examples.
Representing germs on neighborhoods and shrinking when finitely many germs vanish or satisfy identities.
Holomorphic charts and complex-manifold conventions for the analytic structure sheaf.
Exactness conventions in the coherent-module calculus.
Checking constructed kernel generators, epimorphisms and partial resolutions on stalks.
Finite order on the last-coordinate slice, including regularity after translation.
Monicity, positive degree in the bounded-degree reduction, and vanishing lower coefficients at the center.
Preparing all tuple entries in a common coordinate direction and factoring the last polynomial at an arbitrary point.
Holomorphic quotient and polynomial remainder, including uniqueness used to identify polynomial quotients in the bounded-degree proof.
Convergent local expansions, integral-domain arguments and coordinate divisibility in the examples.
Coefficient comparison, integral-domain arguments and divisibility by coordinates.
Choosing a common regular direction by applying the supplier to the product of the nonzero tuple germs.
Noetherianity of the lower-dimensional base germ ring in Oka proof step 6.1.
Finite generation of the coefficient-kernel stalk as a submodule of a finite free module over the Noetherian base germ ring.
The explicit ambient choice assumption in the Oka theorem and examples.

seams_checked.note: The projective GAGA theorem's A3 cites coherence, closure operations and local finite partial resolutions faithfully. Its proof distinguishes the separately supplied algebraic twisting-sheaf resolution from a global analytic free resolution. No reverse prerequisite into this batch was found.

The local acyclicity theorem's F1–F2 preserve the coherence definition, AC assumption and partial-resolution endpoint qualification. Step 1.2 restricts one sufficiently long local resolution to a polydisc; it requires no injectivity at the leftmost free term. No reverse prerequisite was found.

Both examples use coherence of the structure sheaf, finite free modules and their cokernels under AC. These are consequences of the supplied interface; neither example attributes acyclicity itself to Oka coherence. No reverse prerequisite was found.

The section-topology definition uses the coherence definition. The intersection-acyclicity, topology and compact-finiteness proofs accurately restate local finite partial resolutions and closure under kernels and cokernels, retaining AC and the leftmost-term qualification. Intersection acyclicity explicitly assumes its resolution on the relevant neighborhood. No reverse prerequisite was found.

The finite-but-nonzero example retains AC and uses only the valid consequence that a holomorphic line bundle is locally free of rank one and hence coherent. Its cohomology computation has separate suppliers. No reverse prerequisite was found.
